hens_rule_text: Up to 8 domesticated hens on a residential lot of at least 9,000 sq ft in the E-1, R-1, R-1A, R-2 and R-2A zoning districts, with a permit.
permit_notes: A domesticated hen permit from the Clarksville Building and Codes Department is required before keeping hens; the application references a one-time fee of $50. Other fowl and poultry (ducks, geese, quail, pigeons, turkeys) do not qualify as domesticated hens and are not covered by this permit.
setback_notes: Search extracts of the code describe the coop and enclosure as located in the rear of the property, at least 10 ft from any side property line; no distance from a neighbor's dwelling was found.
coop_rules: Hens kept outside any habitable structure in a fenced enclosure with a covered coop inside it. Coop: at least 2 sq ft per hen, maximum 50 sq ft. Enclosure (including the coop): at least 6 sq ft per hen, maximum 400 sq ft total. Must be kept clean; waste removed at least biweekly.
zoning_notes: Allowed only in residential zoning districts E-1, R-1, R-1A, R-2 and R-2A on lots of at least 9,000 sq ft. Breeding of permitted hens on the property is prohibited.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: Clarksville, TN Code of Ordinances, Title 3 Animals (hosted copy)
Title 3, Animals, Clarksville, TN Code of Ordinances (Municode)
Domesticated Hen Application, Clarksville Building & Codes Department

research_notes: Facts come from WebSearch extracts quoting the Municode section 3-109 text (lot size, hen count, coop and enclosure dimensions, rooster and slaughter bans) and from a search extract of the city's hen permit application referencing a $50 fee; the Municode page and the PDF permit form could not be opened directly (PDF fetch returned binary/blocked), so the exact setback-from-dwelling distance and full permit process were not independently confirmed.
